A.why: One coherent comparative recycling decision: explain the two transformation routes sufficiently to judge which meets the same stated product demand under supplied quality/yield/energy/cost constraints. Arithmetic and evidence limits support that single decision. This does not add an independently executable recycling recipe, full LCA, hydrolysis mechanism or general process-engineering competence. The ordinary goal has no examData, memory routine or orientation completion meaning.

P.why: e1 chain/model understanding, e2 equivalent functional denominator and consistent inventory, e3 reasoned conditional evaluation each have observable demands and case-specific rubrics. PMMA/MMA identity/repeat-unit model and quantitative data are completely supplied. The second case changes usable-quality constraints, requires virgin blend input and inverse yield calculation, and gives a true energy/cost trade-off; repeating A ranking fails. No actual experiment or learner evidence is asserted.
P.taskCountBoundary: Two available full cases and profile minimumIndependentDemonstrations2 represent genuine independent understanding/transfer; they are not a compulsory count of two separately labelled tasks. A coherent multi-step performance can supply enough evidence; stop when all aspects are shown.
P.chemicalModel: PMMA repeat unit[–CH2–C(CH3)(COOCH3)–]n and MMA CH2=C(CH3)–C(=O)–O–CH3 correspond. Depolymerisation can recover polymerisable MMA under suitable conditions; no all-polymers-to-monomers or quantitative recovery guarantee is made. End groups/side reactions are explicitly omitted.
P.languageParity: DE/EN have the same model, 100kg inputs, output quantities, boundaries, quality data, tasks, solutions and scoring; no material translation changes the judgment.

independentCaseSolutions.reasoning: Use final qualified PMMA, not the80kg intermediate MMA, as denominator. Both final materials meet the same supplied transparent-sheet specification. Mechanical is provisionally lower in measured operating energy/cost; this is not a complete ecological ranking. Upstream inputs, residue treatment, energy-source/emission differences and other missing stages limit an always claim; vendor interest warrants source scrutiny.
independentCaseSolutions.rubric: 3points distinguish chain retention, chain cleavage to givenMMA and purification/repolymerisation;4points for four normalised values;3points conditional choice/whole-environmental limit/claim and source assessment. Rounding and alternative bounded weighting are allowed. No automatic mastery from10points.

independentCaseSolutions.reasoning: 42MPa regranulate alone fails45MPa. The75:25blend is experimentally given as48MPa and is not an invented linear strength interpolation;47MPa monomer-routePMMA also qualifies. Account for manufacturing15kg virgin material and blending. Different waste inputs are appropriate for the same qualified60kg output. Neither received waste mass nor adding virgin material proves a closed loss-free loop. Both conditional choices can be justified with explicit weighting and missing environmental data.
independentCaseSolutions.rubric: 2points chain explanation/yield and virgin-input limits;5points stated quantity/balance groups, with transparent follow-on error credit;3points same-specification/real3Euro-vs9kWh conflict/claim boundaries. Ten points total; no winner forced.

M.why: Current performance is reading a supplied chemical model and quantities, explaining transformation and weighing a conditional same-function decision. Compact polymer/thermoplastic foundations are available through real ordinary priors; supplied PMMA/MMA names/formulas, numerical process conditions, yields and prices do not justify memorisation or a new recall deck. No SRS unit is required just to turn this new ordinary row green.
